correctness.rationale: For q,k>=2 and n=kq+1 the cyclic-gap inequality for the distance power C_n^{q-1} gives alpha=k. In a maximum independent k-set the k cyclic steps are q except one q+1, so the complete list is I_j={j,j+q,...,j+(k-1)q} and contains n distinct sets. Since gcd(q,n)=1, the step-q cyclic relabelling sends these to all length-k intervals. Their hitting sets are exactly the subsets with positive cyclic gaps <=k. Rooted circular gap counting gives H_{q,k}(z)=sum_{t=q+1}^n (n/t)[u^n](u+...+u^k)^t z^t. The min t=q+1 case has deficits summing k-1, hence coefficient n/(q+1)*binom(k+q-1,q). Boundaries q=k=2 and all t up to n are covered. Independent brute-subset enumeration and a separately written bounded-composition count agreed on five (q,k) pairs, including (2,3,7) with 14 minimum transversals and (3,3,10) with 25. These finite tests corroborate but do not prove universal quantifiers.
